bullets.title: Momentum bounce: SOX rebounds sharply after 11%+ two-day drawdown; AI capex narrative drives tape
bullets.body: US equities finished higher Monday with the momentum factor outperforming; the SOX rebounded sharply following an 11%+ two-day decline. AI infrastructure optimism — anchored by the TeraWulf/Anthropic $19B lease and AVGO/AAPL ASIC extension — was cited as the primary catalyst. Equal-weight S&P trailed by ~70bp, and consumer-facing groups remained under pressure.

bullets.title: Fed Gov. Waller hawkish pivot: inflation risks have 'completely flipped' from labor market concerns
bullets.body: Waller signaled a decisive tone shift, stating risks have 'completely flipped' from 2024-25 labor market concerns to rising inflation after 9 months of consistent overshoot. He warned that price shocks now transmit multiple times larger impacts to sticky prices than pre-COVID, and questioned the utility of rigid dot-plot forward guidance. JPMorgan sees risks to Treasury yields skewed higher over the medium term.

bullets.title: June ISM Services in line but softening; employment component back in expansion
bullets.body: June ISM Services headline slipped to 54.0 from 54.5, meeting consensus but declining month-over-month. Employment jumped to 51.2 from 47.9 (vs. 48.2 consensus), returning to expansion for the first time in four months. Prices paid declined from 71.3 to 67.7, driven by lower energy prices.

bullets.title: NFP miss reinforces labor softening narrative, though market digesting conflicting signals
bullets.body: Citi flagged the NFP consensus miss as signaling a weaker job market and a potential dovish Fed pivot with slowing wage growth. However, Waller's hawkish tone on inflation and the ISM services employment rebound complicate the picture, leaving the macro regime in flux.

bullets.title: Hedgeye July CPI nowcast at +3.54% y/y; oil normalization driving headline disinflation
bullets.body: Hedgeye's July inflation nowcast prints +3.54% y/y, down 29bp sequentially, with June estimated at +3.83% y/y (-42bp sequential). Oil price normalization is the primary driver of headline disinflation; Middle East energy volatility remains the key rate-of-change risk. The model has 90% directional accuracy on CPI acceleration/deceleration.

bullets.title: Treasury supply heavy this week; 3-year auction faces less favorable setup
bullets.body: Treasury sells ~$120B this week in 3-, 10-, and 30-year auctions. JPMorgan expects the $58B 3-year auction to require greater concession: 3-year yields are 5bp below June auction levels but the sector has richened to fairly valued/modestly rich, and the WI roll opened at +0.75bp cheaper than fair value. Front-end yields fell 1-2bp Monday; curve steepened 2bp.

bullets.title: Anthropic $19B/20-yr data center lease anchors AI infrastructure narrative; WULF and IREN surge
bullets.body: TeraWulf signed a 20-year, 401MW lease with Anthropic at its Justified Data Campus in Kentucky generating ~$19B in contracted revenue, with implied rent of $197/kW/month well above prior estimates of $150/kW/month and an ~18% development yield. WULF +4.9% on the session; IREN gained ~13% on AI capacity demand sentiment. Anthropic was also separately reported to be in talks for 1.4GW+ of Australian data center capacity.

bullets.title: AI capex boom narrative faces macro scrutiny; China AI risk to US equity moats flagged
bullets.body: One macro analyst disputes claims that AI capex drove >50% of US GDP growth, citing chain-weighting errors and endogenous trade drag. More pointedly, the note warns that if China releases cheap AI and bridges the moat of US AI leaders, it would directly hit their equity valuations — and signals that spending discipline may be approaching given how extended AI capex looks.

bullets.title: IB activity surging into 2Q26 earnings season; M&A +64% YoY, IPOs +353% YoY
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's deal dashboard shows global IB volumes broadly accelerating in 2Q26: announced M&A up 64% YoY (completed +33%), ECM/IPOs up 107%/353% YoY, and DCM up 19% YoY. Global M&A reached $2.8T in 1H 2026 with a record 47 deals valued at $10B+. Bank earnings kick off July 14 with C, GS, JPM, and WFC; management expected to reiterate pipeline positivity.

bullets.title: Comm Equipment surges +2.6% as AI networking gains accelerate; ANET +8.3%
bullets.body: The Comm Equipment sub-sector led tech Monday at +2.6%, with Arista Networks up 8.3% and Ciena +2.7% on AI networking tailwinds. Semiconductors gained +2.2% with CPU, GPU, and analog names leading; semi-cap equipment and comm chips lagged. Software was nearly flat (+0.2%), held back by MSFT (-1.0%), DDOG (-1.9%), ADBE (-0.8%), and CRM (-0.3%).

bullets.title: MSFT CoPilot AI orchestration layer underappreciated; Azure acceleration expected in 3 weeks
bullets.body: One analyst reiterates high-conviction Buy on MSFT, arguing the market is not crediting its CoPilot orchestration layer — which routes enterprise queries across AI models and allows switching without disruption. MSFT is expected to report Azure acceleration and capex deceleration driving cash flow growth at earnings in ~3 weeks.

bullets.title: NVDA next-gen AI rack system delayed to 2028 on manufacturing issues with circuit board
bullets.body: Nvidia's next-generation AI rack system has been pushed back to 2028 due to manufacturing challenges with the circuit board. This was noted as a risk event within the broader semi/AI infrastructure rally on Monday.

bullets.title: Renewables outperform sharply: BE +8.9%, ENPH +3.4%, GEV +3.5%; S&P Utilities -1.1%
bullets.body: Renewables sub-sectors significantly outperformed broader utilities Monday: Bloom Energy +8.9%, GEV +3.5%, Enph +3.4%, Global X Hydrogen ETF +2.4%, Invesco Solar ETF +2.2%. The S&P 500 Utilities Index declined 1.1% as traditional utilities lagged. Deutsche Bank upgraded FSLR to Buy with a $272 PT (from $245), adding a catalyst for solar.

bullets.title: Office REIT fears over AI job losses fading; Evercore ISI favors CDP, CUZ for 2H26 visibility
bullets.body: Evercore ISI notes that concerns about AI-driven mass tech layoffs in office demand have abated following robust jobs data, and sees Office REITs outperforming in Q2. They prefer CDP and CUZ for earnings visibility and KRC as a West Coast/SF recovery play; downgraded SLG to in-line on valuation after Q2 outperformance.

bullets.title: Communications Services +1.6% led by META and GOOGL; advertising sub-sector +2.7%
bullets.body: The S&P 1500 Communications Services Index gained 1.6% on Monday, with META and GOOGL leading. The advertising sub-sector was the strongest at +2.7%, supported by AI capex optimism. Cable/Pay TV and Media Conglomerates were the weakest at -1.9%, dragged by NFLX, DIS, and CMCSA.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo: Google search sessions +35% YoY in 2Q26; holding share vs ChatGPT
bullets.body: Wells Fargo data shows global search category session growth accelerated from low-single-digit % in 4Q24 to 35% YoY in 2Q26, with Google maintaining market share vs. ChatGPT over the past 12 months. Expanding use cases and AI search are driving growth; Google also has supply surplus enabling ad load reduction in AI search products, a potential monetization lever.

bullets.title: Specialty retail coverage resumed at Morgan Stanley: bullish on M, VSXY; underweight LULU, KSS
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley resumed specialty retail and department store coverage with an improving 2H26 backdrop thesis. Overweight on Macy's (M, +1.8%) approaching a flat-to-positive sales inflection, and VSXY on turnaround durability. Underweight on LULU (-2.4%) where the Street underestimates the depth of the Americas reset, and KSS (-7.0%) where revenue recovery is being prematurely priced in.

bullets.title: White House deregulatory push: eliminate 702 administrative rules, project $1.5T in savings
bullets.body: The White House is planning a deregulatory push targeting the elimination of 702 administrative rules with projected savings of $1.5T. This was flagged as a potential tail catalyst for financials and broader risk sentiment.

bullets.title: Anthropic warns Congress: Chinese AI (Alibaba) catching up via distillation; export controls on Claude lifted
bullets.body: Anthropic warned US lawmakers that Chinese AI models, specifically Alibaba's, are catching up to frontier US models via AI distillation techniques. Separately, the DOJ lifted export controls on Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Alibaba also reportedly banned employee use of Claude Code internally.
